meta.description: Yes — George W. Bush said it. His unscripted Ground Zero “bullhorn” reply to rescue workers on Sept. 14, 2001, confirmed in the official White House transcript.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'I can hear you! The rest of the world hears you! And the people who knocked these buildings down will hear all of us soon!'?
meta.ogDescription: Yes — George W. Bush, atop the rubble at Ground Zero, Sept. 14, 2001. The unscripted bullhorn reply, confirmed in the official White House transcript.

answer.label: Spoken by
answer.authorDates: b. 1946 · 43rd President of the United States (2001–2009)
answer.sourceLine: An unusual case for a “magnet” name — he really said it. Bush spoke these words extemporaneously through a bullhorn atop the World Trade Center rubble on 14 September 2001, replying to a rescue worker who shouted that he couldn’t hear him. The wording is confirmed in the official White House transcript.

source.heading: The source

docMeta.dd: “Bullhorn” remarks to rescue workers at Ground Zero
President George W. Bush, standing beside retired FDNY firefighter Bob Beckwith
World Trade Center site, Murray & West Streets, New York City

source.excerpt: America today is on bended knee in prayer for the people whose lives were lost here… [a rescue worker: “I can’t hear you!”] I can hear you! I can hear you! The rest of the world hears you! And the people who knocked these buildings down will hear all of us soon!
trail: The official White House release “President Bush Salutes Heroes in New York” records the exact exchange, dated 14 Sept. 2001 at Murray & West Streets.
American Rhetoric and Speakola both host the full transcript of the bullhorn address.
Bob Beckwith, the firefighter who handed Bush the bullhorn and stood at his side, told NBC New York that the President “changed his whole speech and made it up as he was going.”
source.cutTag: stylized from the official White House transcript
source.excerptNote: The line was unscripted: aides had prepared brief condolences, but when workers yelled that they couldn’t hear him, Bush answered off the cuff and the site erupted in chants of “U.S.A.!”

author.bio: George Walker Bush served as the 43rd President of the United States from 2001 to 2009. The defining event of his first year was the 11 September 2001 terrorist attacks; three days later he visited the smoking ruins of the World Trade Center, where his impromptu bullhorn reply to rescue workers became one of the most recognized moments of his presidency.

misattribution.heading: A note on wording
misattribution.intro: The attribution here is genuine — but the popular one-sentence version smooths over how the moment actually unfolded.

items.why: Circulating versions render it as one tidy line. The transcript shows Bush actually said “I can hear you” twice, answering rescue workers who shouted that they couldn’t hear him on the spot, not reading a script.
The official White House text uses plain periods; the exclamation points come from how the emotional delivery is usually re-typed. The words themselves are accurate.

misattribution.truthLine: The line is authentically George W. Bush’s, spoken through a bullhorn at Ground Zero on 14 Sept. 2001 and preserved in the official transcript.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Three days after the attacks, Bush toured the still-burning wreckage of the World Trade Center. Aides had planned only a few quiet words of condolence. When workers deep in the pile shouted that they couldn’t hear him, Bush — his arm around retired firefighter Bob Beckwith — abandoned the script and shouted back.
The reply, and the roar of “U.S.A.!” that followed, became the emotional high point of his early presidency and is remembered as the “bullhorn moment.”
detailsBody: The bullhorn Bush used is now a featured artifact in the collection of the George W. Bush Presidential Library.
